messages:
alex: Quick note 1 1 — noticed inconsistent timeout naming across docs: Python uses `timeout_seconds`, JS shows `deadlineMs`, and some snippets use `--timeout-secs`. This is confusing for users. Can we pick a single convention for copy/paste examples?

mira: I vote `timeout_ms` for quickstarts and HTTP examples. Makes unit explicit.

sam: +1. For Go examples keep `context.WithTimeout` but add an inline comment like `// equivalent to timeout_ms=3000`.

lena: Streaming caveat: client-side timeout cancels the local read loop; server may still proceed generating tokens. Add a short note in streaming docs and errref so users know the difference vs `Retry-After`.

alex: Plan: mira updates snippets and quickstarts; sam runs snippet-lint; lena patches streaming docs; alex will grep for `deadline` and `timeout_seconds` in errref. Aim to merge this week.

docs-bot: docs-bot: Created PR checklist: [ ] unify snippets to `timeout_ms`, [ ] add Go mapping comment, [ ] streaming cancel caveat, [ ] update errref conversion table, [ ] snippet-lint + link-check.

mira: WIP PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2401 1 replaced mixed params in 10 files and added a small conversion table. Left TODO where embedded Gists need manual update.

sam: Running snippet-lint now; found two occurrences inside a Gist and one shell quickstart using `--timeout-secs`. I'll update in review.

lena: I'll add the streaming paragraph in errref and mark it in the PR comments. Suggest wording: "Client timeout = client abort; server `Retry-After` = server-advised retry window. They are distinct"

alex: Thanks. If CI or the link-check flags SDK param docs, we'll add a short mapping note in the SDK reference. Target merge Thurs EOD. Flag here if blocked.
